name: vendored-artifact-upstream-route
title: Vendored-artifact defects have no recorded route to upstream
description: Eight active tasks rediscover the same constraint: the defect they describe lives in a file installed from sd-ai-command-pack or upstream Trellis, so the fix is an upstream pull request that this repository's run-level authority cannot approve. Each re-derives ownership from a different registry and each stalls at the same undocumented boundary. Record the ownership lookup, the upstream route, and the local-only fallback once.
creator: sdelmas
notes: Consolidates a constraint eight active tasks each re-derived: 08-06-finalization-ordering-trap, 08-06-prism-rules-lane-divergence, 08-06-sd-review-local-rebuttal-gap, 08-06-watch-coordinator-infra-classification, 08-06-task-create-base-branch-default, 08-06-task-json-trailing-newline, 08-07-status-collector-pack-drift, and 08-07-review-py-local-fork. The first six reached it independently before this task existed; the seventh and eighth were authored after it and still had to restate the whole constraint, because a filed task is not recorded guidance. The eighth is the one case where the fix already exists locally in an install: "always" file, so its local-only outcome expires at the next pack refresh rather than being stable. The prd.md table is the canonical membership list; a new member is added by appending a row there, and this task.json must be updated in the same edit. Three registries decide ownership (.sd-ai-command-pack/manifest.json, its provenance.json, and .trellis/.template-hashes.json) with no single lookup across them. Two non-obvious behaviours must be captured: install: if-not-exists means repo-owned after first install (this is how .prism/rules.json is classified, and it changed the prism task's remedy from 'clobbered' to 'undelivered'), and .github/copilot-instructions.md is dual-owned, so its Trellis hash reports permanent drift that is not drift. Sequencing: eleven active tasks edit .trellis/spec/backend/quality-guidelines.md; this is one of them, at order 5 in the P2 band, ahead of the rest of the cluster (10-70), because it defines the shared ownership section those tasks each extend. Cluster membership is decided by the PRD's stated deliverable -- a Requirement or acceptance criterion that writes to that file -- not by whether implement.jsonl lists it, since the manifest is a read-for-context list and several non-cluster tasks cite the file as a contract to read.
